answer: The Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm, akin to navigating a treacherous canyon, can effectively resist fake-identity attacks by implementing a voting mechanism that requires agents to be in a consensus range, akin to traversing the tundra, to be considered valid. This range, or "ridge," is set by the network, and any agent attempting to fake an identity must accumulate sufficient computational power to breach the ridge, thereby incurring significant costs and rendering the attack futile.
